info.title: CONVO API
info.description: The pinned contract for the implemented CONVO v1 HTTP surface.

200.description: Authenticated session; returns hardened session and CSRF cookies

post.description: Re-authenticates with the current password, replaces it with an Argon2id hash, retains the current session, revokes every other session, and writes account-level audit evidence in one transaction.

204.description: Password changed; current session retained and other sessions revoked.

post.description: Always returns 202 with the same body, whether or not the address has an account and whether or not the request was rate limited (IAM-03). The token is delivered out of band and never appears in a response.

202.description: Accepted. Says nothing about whether the account exists.

post.summary: Complete password recovery and revoke every session
post.description: Consumes the single-use challenge, replaces the password and revokes every session for the account in one transaction. Expired, already used and never issued all return the same 400.

204.description: Password replaced; all sessions revoked and the caller's cookies cleared.

get.summary: Read the current authenticated principal and session
List active sessions owned by the current user
Read an active session owned by the current user

delete.summary: Revoke an active session owned by the current user

204.description: Session revoked; current-session cookies are cleared when applicable

get.summary: Read the public installation descriptor

post.summary: Create the first company and Owner exactly once
Accept an invitation and join the company
post.description: Unauthenticated by necessity: the invitee may have no account yet, so the token is the only thing identifying the request. It is single-use, short-lived and rate limited for that reason, and it appears in the path, so access logs must redact it (see docs/security/threat-model.md). Unknown, expired, revoked, already-used and wrong-password all return the same 400: distinguishing them would make this an account-existence oracle for the invited address.

get.summary: List the current user's active company memberships

200.description: Active memberships resolved through tenant RLS

get.summary: List channel connections
get.description: Every connection with its readiness, its capability matrix and the separate pieces of evidence behind it. Requires `channel.manage`. A caller with no membership in this company receives 404, not 403.

post.description: Claims the asset for this company installation-wide, stores the credential encrypted, and returns a connection in `authorization_needed`. Connecting does not make a channel work: every later state needs its own evidence. Requires `channel.manage`, CSRF and an `Idempotency-Key` — a retried connect that minted a second connection would leave two rows racing for the same inbound messages.

201.description: The connection, which is not yet working.

409.description: The asset is already connected, or the Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request. Whether the asset is held by this company or another one is deliberately indistinguishable.

delete.description: Revokes every credential for the connection and releases the asset claim so the same asset can be connected again. The connection row and its event history stay: they are evidence. Requires `channel.manage` and CSRF. Disconnecting twice succeeds.

post.description: Stores a new credential version and supersedes the previous one, which is kept so a credential in flight during the rotation can still be identified. Verification is reset: the new token has proved nothing yet. Requires `credential.rotate` — reaching a provider credential is a narrower act than managing a channel — and CSRF.

200.description: The connection, with a new credential fingerprint and verification cleared.

503.description: Credential storage is not configured in this installation.

get.summary: List outbound messages on a channel
get.description: Requires `conversation.read`.

200.description: The messages with their command state, delivery state and attempts.

post.description: Writes the command and its outbox entry in one transaction and answers **202** — durably queued, and nothing sent. The permit that decides whether it may actually go out is re-evaluated by the dispatcher at the moment of dispatch, because a window that is open now can be shut by then. Only what would be pointless to queue is refused here: a channel that cannot carry the message type, and a private note. Requires `conversation.reply` and CSRF.

202.description: Durably queued. Nothing has been sent.

409.description: The channel is disconnected and cannot send.

422.description: The message can never be delivered on this channel: an unsupported type, a template the channel has no concept of, or a private note. Typed rather than queued to fail later.

post.summary: Synchronize the WhatsApp template catalogue from Meta
post.description: Fetches all pages from the connected WhatsApp Business Account, upserts current templates, and disables templates no longer returned. Requires channel.manage and CSRF.

post.summary: Ask the provider whether the stored credential works
post.description: The only operation that may record `credential_verified`. With no provider transport configured it records `provider_not_connected` — which is the honest answer, not a failure of the request. Requires `channel.manage` and CSRF.

200.description: The connection with the result of the check recorded on it.

503.description: Credential storage is not configured in this installation.

get.summary: List the channels this build can serve
get.description: Every channel kind with its capability matrix and whether this build has an adapter for it. Requires `channel.manage`.

get.summary: List contacts
get.description: Requires `contact.read`. `q` filters on the display name only — there is no fuzzy identity search, because a search that matched on a similar number would be the identity inference the model refuses (CT-03).

get.summary: Read one contact with its identities, consent and suppressions
get.description: Requires `contact.read`. Consent is returned newest-first as evidence, not as a flag. Suppressions are returned beside it because a suppression **outranks** any consent (CT-08), and an operator looking at a granted consent needs to see the thing that overrides it.

patch.description: The display name and the business attributes, and nothing else. An identity is not editable here: changing which number reaches a person is a different act with different consequences. Requires `contact.edit`, which an Agent holds only for the contacts of conversations they are in.

post.description: Appends a record; it never edits one. Withdrawal is a new row, so the history stays answerable. Two refusals are part of the contract: `import_is_not_consent` (422) because a row in a spreadsheet is not somebody agreeing to be messaged (CT-07), and `suppression_outranks_consent` (409) because lifting an opt-out needs an explicit opt-in workflow this build does not offer (CT-08, CT-13). Requires `consent.record`.

201.description: The contact, with the new record on its history.

get.summary: List the conversations this caller may read
get.description: Returns a cursor-paged, authorization-scoped InboxQuery result. Every record passed `conversation.read` before the final keyset LIMIT. `filter` is a repeatable JSON-encoded object using the documented closed filter catalogue; it never accepts SQL fields, operators, or sort fragments. `queue=mine` (the default) returns the caller's own conversations; `queue=all` returns everything within their reach, which for an Agent is still only their own.

schema.description: Repeatable JSON object: { key, operator, value?, fieldId? }. Keys: status, assignment_state, assigned_agent_id, team_id, channel, connection_id, label_id, priority, unread, unreplied, created_at, last_activity_at, waiting_since, customer_name, customer_phone, collaborator_id, participant_id, handoff_target_id, custom_field.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Case-insensitive search over conversation UUID, contact name, phone, and peer identity.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque signed keyset cursor bound to tenant, effective query, and sort.

get.summary: List the Unassigned queue as projected cards
get.description: Requires `conversation.unassigned.preview`. Returns queue cards only: conversation id, inbox label, channel, masked display label, priority, status, wait time and claim availability. Never a snippet, a timeline, a note, an attachment or contact PII — the projection happens on the server, not in the browser.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: Limit the queue to one channel connection.

get.summary: List agents visible to the supervisor
Read conversations in an agent workload using the supervisor's own scope
Read current scoped workload for one agent

200.description: Current workload, scoped by the supervisor principal

get.summary: Read one conversation
get.description: Requires `conversation.read` for this conversation. An agent whose grant is scoped to their own work is refused before a claim and allowed after one; losing inbox access overrides both.

post.description: Atomic and version-checked. Requires `conversation.claim`. Send the version shown on the card; if somebody else claimed it first the answer is 409 `conversation_version_conflict` rather than a silent takeover.

post.summary: Move a conversation through its lifecycle
post.description: Wait, snooze, resolve, reopen or archive. One endpoint because it is one decision: the lifecycle table answers all five, and splitting them across routes would let a future route answer differently. Waiting and snoozing need `conversation.reply`; resolving, reopening and archiving need `conversation.close`. Every command is fenced on the version the caller saw and answers 409 `conversation_version_conflict` on a stale one. A move the table refuses is a 409 naming the reason (`already_open`, `not_resolved`, `archived_conversation_is_immutable`, `not_waiting_on_a_customer`); an invalid snooze is a 422 (`wake_time_in_the_past`, `wake_time_too_far_ahead`, `unknown_timezone`).

get.summary: The reporting episodes of a conversation
get.description: Oldest first. Requires `conversation.read` for the conversation.

get.summary: The private notes on a conversation
get.description: Requires `conversation.note` — not merely `conversation.read`. An analyst who may read conversations for reporting has no business reading what colleagues said to each other about a customer.

post.description: Requires `conversation.note`. The note never enters the outbound path, does not reopen the conversation, does not mark a customer reply delivered and does not reset the channel window.

Unread is a fact about a person: this moves only the caller's cursor and is never a provider receipt. The cursor only moves forward, so opening an old conversation cannot un-read the newer part of it.

patch.description: Only the author. A note is attributed speech, and an edit by somebody else would leave a sentence standing under a name that did not write it. The edit is marked; 403 `not_the_author` otherwise.

delete.description: Only the author. The row is kept and marked rather than removed: a note that vanished without trace is a note somebody can deny having written, and the colleague who acted on it could not show what they read.

200.description: The note, marked deleted and stripped of its text.

get.summary: Read one page of a conversation's timeline
get.description: Inbound events and outbound commands merged for reading and returned oldest-first within the page. Authorized exactly like reading the conversation itself. `cursor` walks **backwards** into the history; it is opaque, signed, bound to this company, this conversation and this sort, and expires — a stale or foreign one is answered `cursor_invalid` or `cursor_expired` with a safe refresh path rather than silently restarting at the top.

post.description: Answers **202** once the command and its outbox row have committed; nothing has been sent yet. Requires `conversation.reply` for this conversation, so an Agent may reply to the conversations they hold and to no others. The recipient comes from the conversation record: a `peerIdentity` in the body is ignored, because an agent permitted to reply to one customer must not be able to reach another by editing a field.

get.summary: List the invitations issued in this company
get.description: Requires `member.manage`. Tokens are never included. A caller with no membership receives 404, not 403.

post.description: Requires `member.manage`, CSRF and an Idempotency-Key. The role and scopes are checked against the inviter's own grants, so nobody can give away reach they do not have. Any live invitation for the same address is superseded, because two valid tokens for one seat would be two ways in. The response never contains the token.

201.description: Created. The token was handed to the delivery port, not returned here.

delete.description: Requires `member.manage` and CSRF. Revoking an invitation that is already accepted or revoked returns 404: there is no pending invitation to act on.

get.summary: Read one outbound message
get.description: Its command state, its delivery state and every attempt. Requires `conversation.read`.

get.summary: List ownership transfer offers
get.description: Requires `member.manage`.

post.description: Requires `tenant.delete` — the one key that separates Owner from Admin, which is what makes "only an Owner may transfer ownership" true without naming the role. One live offer per company; a second returns 409.

delete.summary: Cancel an ownership offer you made
delete.description: Only the offering Owner may cancel.

parameters.name: transferId
parameters.description: Identifier.

post.description: Only the recipient may accept. The outgoing Owner becomes an Admin and the recipient becomes Owner in one transaction; the company is briefly Owner-less between the two updates, which is why the last-Owner constraint is deferred to commit. Anyone who is not the recipient receives 404, because whether an offer is outstanding is not their business.

parameters.name: transferId
parameters.description: Identifier.

post.description: Only the recipient may decline.

parameters.name: transferId
parameters.description: Identifier.

get.summary: List the memberships in this company
get.description: Memberships with their role and scope grants. Requires `member.manage`. A caller with no membership in this company receives 404, not 403: answering 403 would confirm the company exists.

200.description: Memberships with their role and scope grants. Requires `member.manage`. A caller with no membership in this company receives 404, not 403: answering 403 would confirm the company exists.

patch.summary: Change a membership role, status or scopes
patch.description: Requires `member.manage` and CSRF. The delegation ceiling applies: an actor can never produce access wider than their own, which is enforced by comparing grants rather than by naming roles. Suspending or revoking your own membership is refused, and the database refuses any change that would leave the company with no active Owner.

parameters.name: membershipId
parameters.description: Identifier.

get.summary: List the immutable permission catalogue for an authorized company admin

200.description: Permission catalogue after role.manage authorization by key

get.summary: Read one page of the event feed
get.description: Catch-up after being offline. Events are authorized one at a time against the caller's current grants, so a conversation they may only preview arrives as a projected queue card. A cursor issued under different permissions, for another company, or older than the retained window is answered with `reset_required` and its reason rather than a partial resume.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque position from a previous page. Omit to start from the beginning of the retained window.

200.description: A page of events, or an instruction to reset.

get.summary: Subscribe to the event stream
get.description: Server-Sent Events. The session cookie authenticates the connection and the membership decides what it carries; the principal is re-read on every pass, so a revoked membership or a removed inbox stops the stream rather than waiting for the next login. Frame ids are cursors, so `Last-Event-ID` resumes exactly where the connection stopped. The connection is closed deliberately after its maximum age with a `stream_cycled` event.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque position to resume from. `Last-Event-ID` wins over it.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Sent automatically by EventSource on reconnect.

200.description: An event stream. Each frame is one authorized event, a `reset_required` instruction, or a `stream_cycled` notice.

get.summary: List the company roles and the grants each holds
get.description: Roles with their permission keys and scope levels, for an effective-access preview. Requires `role.manage`. A caller with no membership in this company receives 404, not 403: answering 403 would confirm the company exists.

200.description: Roles with their permission keys and scope levels, for an effective-access preview. Requires `role.manage`. A caller with no membership in this company receives 404, not 403: answering 403 would confirm the company exists.

post.description: Requires `role.manage` and CSRF. A custom role may only carry **delegable** keys the actor already holds — the rule that stops a role being minted with `credential.rotate` and then assigned to oneself. Built-in roles are immutable and are not created here.

patch.summary: Replace a custom role’s name, description and grants
patch.description: Requires `role.manage` and CSRF. Editing a built-in role returns 409; the database refuses it too.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Identifier.

delete.summary: Delete a custom role nobody holds
delete.description: Requires `role.manage` and CSRF. A role still held by an active membership returns 409 rather than orphaning those memberships or silently moving people.

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: Identifier.

get.summary: List the teams in this company
get.description: Teams and their membership counts. Requires `member.manage`, because team composition decides who sees which work. A caller with no membership in this company receives 404, not 403: answering 403 would confirm the company exists.

200.description: Teams and their membership counts. Requires `member.manage`, because team composition decides who sees which work. A caller with no membership in this company receives 404, not 403: answering 403 would confirm the company exists.

post.description: Requires `member.manage` and CSRF. A team name is reserved only while the team is live, so an archived name can be reused.

patch.description: Requires `member.manage` and CSRF. Archiving keeps the team's routing history and its membership rows; deleting would take both.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Identifier.

post.summary: Add a membership to a team
post.description: Requires `member.manage` and CSRF. An archived team, or a membership from another company, returns 404.

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Identifier.

delete.summary: Remove a membership from a team

parameters.name: teamId
parameters.description: Identifier.

parameters.name: membershipId
parameters.description: Identifier.

post.summary: Receive a signed Custom Channel delivery
post.description: The versioned contract for a transport CONVO does not write. `version` is required and checked: a payload from a version this build does not implement is kept whole and quarantined for replay rather than parsed hopefully. Contract version 1 defines the event types `message`, `delivery_status` and `read_status`.

parameters.name: X-Convo-Signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA-256 over `<X-Convo-Timestamp>.<raw body>` with this connection’s signing key, hex-encoded. The timestamp is inside the signed material so it cannot be rewritten to make an old capture look fresh.

parameters.name: X-Convo-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds. Deliveries more than 300 seconds old are refused.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Checked against the connection’s declared origins for Website Chat. Matched exactly, never by suffix.

400.description: A verified sender sent a body that will not parse.

401.description: The signature did not verify, or the delivery is outside the replay window.

403.description: The delivery came from an origin this installation has not declared.

404.description: No live asset with that id. Deliberately the same answer a disconnected one gives: an id that exists is not something an unauthenticated caller learns.

429.description: This connection is delivering faster than its configured rate.

503.description: The connection holds no signing key, so nothing can be verified.

get.summary: Answer the provider subscription challenge
get.description: Echoes `hub.challenge` when `hub.verify_token` matches the stored hash. Proving we hold the verify token is all this does: it authenticates nothing on a POST.

403.description: The challenge failed. A wrong token, a wrong mode and a missing challenge are deliberately indistinguishable.

post.description: Verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` over the **exact raw request bytes** in constant time, refuses a replayed delivery, resolves the company from the verified asset inside the payload — never from a header, a path parameter or a query string — and journals the raw envelope before answering. A 200 means the delivery is durably journaled and nothing more.

requestBody.description: The provider envelope, verified as bytes before it is parsed.

202.description: Verified and understood, with nothing here to route: an asset no company has connected, or an envelope carrying no asset. Retrying cannot change that, so it is not a failure.

400.description: A verified sender sent a body that will not parse. Retrying cannot help.

401.description: The signature did not verify, or the delivery is outside the replay window.

503.description: The provider app secret is not configured here. Our fault, and worth retrying once it is fixed — so it is never a silent 200.

post.description: The widget signs each delivery with the key issued to its installation. The installation id in the path selects the key; it never decides who the delivery belongs to — the company comes from the registry row that id resolves to, and nothing is stored unless the signature holds. An origin allowlist and a per-connection rate limit stand in for the protections a provider would otherwise give.

parameters.name: X-Convo-Signature
parameters.description: HMAC-SHA-256 over `<X-Convo-Timestamp>.<raw body>` with this connection’s signing key, hex-encoded. The timestamp is inside the signed material so it cannot be rewritten to make an old capture look fresh.

parameters.name: X-Convo-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds. Deliveries more than 300 seconds old are refused.

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Checked against the connection’s declared origins for Website Chat. Matched exactly, never by suffix.

requestBody.description: `{"object":"web_chat","installation_id":"…","events":[…]}`. Event types: `message` and `session_start`; anything else is stored and shown as a documented fallback.

400.description: A verified sender sent a body that will not parse.

401.description: The signature did not verify, or the delivery is outside the replay window.

403.description: The delivery came from an origin this installation has not declared.

404.description: No live installation with that id. Deliberately the same answer a disconnected one gives: an id that exists is not something an unauthenticated caller learns.

429.description: This connection is delivering faster than its configured rate.

503.description: The connection holds no signing key, so nothing can be verified.

post.summary: Assign or reassign a conversation to a named person
post.description: Requires `conversation.assign`, checked by key and effective scope. The target’s eligibility is re-derived inside the write transaction, so a directory result is a suggestion and never an authorization. A stale `version` is 409 `conversation_version_conflict` rather than a silent takeover; an ineligible target is 422 `assignee_not_eligible`, deliberately the same answer for a missing, foreign and out-of-scope membership so the endpoint is not a membership enumeration oracle. The previous assignee keeps their recorded participation.

200.description: The conversation, as it now stands.

get.summary: The people who could actually take a conversation
get.description: Eligibility is computed the same way the assignment endpoint computes it — by loading each candidate’s principal and asking `authorize` — so the picker and the check cannot disagree. Deliberately not `GET /people`, which requires `member.manage` and returns roles, scopes and login emails: a Supervisor may route work and may not administer memberships. The presentation fields are an allowlist.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The conversation the assignee is for. The master inventory spells this `inbox_id`; the conversation is passed instead so the server evaluates the real target, including its team and its current assignee (recorded in operation-inventory.md).

get.summary: The handoff offers on a conversation, newest first

post.summary: Offer the conversation to a named colleague
post.description: An offer, not a transfer (ADR-0017): while it is pending the current assignee is still the assignee. Requires `conversation.handoff.request`, which an Agent holds at `own` scope so they can offer their own conversation without being able to reassign anybody else’s. At most one live offer per conversation, enforced by a partial unique index — a second is 409 `handoff_already_pending`.

post.summary: Accept, decline or withdraw a handoff offer
post.description: Only the named recipient may accept or decline; only the requester, or somebody who could have made the assignment outright, may cancel. Acceptance settles the offer **and** applies the reassignment in one transaction, fenced on the conversation version at that moment — so an offer made against a conversation that has since moved cannot take it from whoever holds it now. Decline, cancel and expiry change no assignment at all.

patch.summary: Change the queue position a conversation argues for
patch.description: Governed by `conversation.assign`: business-rules.md §7’s row is "Assign others / override routing", and priority is routing (ADR-0017). A dedicated route rather than a general `PATCH /conversations/{id}`, whose authorization would depend on which keys happen to be in the body. Version-fenced and recorded in append-only audit evidence with the previous value.

200.description: The conversation, as it now stands.

get.summary: The people invited to help with a conversation

post.summary: Invite somebody to help with a conversation
post.description: An access-granting act, so the target is validated exactly as an assignment target is. Recorded as an interval rather than a row in `conversation_participants`, which records who actually acted and is never rewritten.

delete.description: Ends the invitation, for the future only. Whatever this person actually did stays on the record and keeps giving them permitted read access to it — historical participation is never erased to make a removal look tidy.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The conversation version the operator saw. In the query because a DELETE carries no body.

BootstrapToken.name: X-Bootstrap-Token
BootstrapToken.description: Installer-provisioned secret accepted only by the one-time bootstrap operation.

CsrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
CsrfToken.description: Must equal the convo_csrf cookie value for state-changing authenticated requests.

RequestId.description: The accepted or server-generated request identifier.

SessionCookies.description: convo_session is HttpOnly; convo_csrf is readable by the same-origin client. Both are Secure in HTTPS deployments and SameSite=Strict.

Error.description: A safe typed failure. HTTP status carries failure semantics.

error.message: The installation bootstrap request is not valid.

details.message: A valid owner email is required.

RateLimited.description: The shared database login limit was exceeded.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the current window expires.

AcceptInvitationRequest.description: The password creates the identity when the address has no account, and proves it when it does. Without it, holding the link would be enough to attach an established account to a company.

CapabilityMatrix.description: What a channel can carry, for one pinned provider version. Read by the UI to enable, disable and explain options.

windowHours.description: Reply window in hours, or null where the channel has none.

templates.description: A WhatsApp concept. False for Messenger and Instagram, which is what stops a WhatsApp template being accepted for them.

readReceipts.description: Absent support renders as `not_available`, never as false or 0%.

implemented.description: Whether this build has an adapter for the kind. False is not a hidden channel.

external_asset_id.description: The provider asset: a phone number id, a Page id, an Instagram account id.

credential_held.description: Whether a credential is stored. Never the credential, never a prefix of it.

credential_fingerprint.description: An HMAC fingerprint that identifies the stored credential without revealing it, so a rotation is visibly a rotation.

provider_app_id.description: Provider-facing app ID used by this connection. Public identifier only; no secret or token is returned.

observed_at.description: When the thing that observed it observed it — not when a form was submitted.

ChannelKind.description: The five channels. WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram are separate products with separate hosts, tokens, scopes, windows and capabilities; nothing is inherited between them.

ChannelReadiness.description: Derived from evidence, never set by hand. `healthy` requires every evidence item; a non-empty token field proves none of them.

ChannelSettings.description: Per-connection configuration for the channels CONVO hosts itself. Meaningless for a provider channel, where identity, callers and rate limits belong to the provider.

origins.description: Whole origins a widget may deliver from, matched exactly. An empty or absent list is read as "not configured yet", which the ingress treats as no — an unconfigured allowlist is not an open one.

ratePerMinute.description: Deliveries per minute for this connection. Defaults to 120.

declaredTypes.description: What a Custom Channel's own transport says it can carry. Intersected with the capability matrix, which is the ceiling: declaring more widens nothing.

CommandState.description: What we did. Unordered: this is not a progress bar. `outcome_unknown` means the request was on the wire and no answer came back — it may have sent, and nothing resends it automatically.

accessToken.description: For a provider channel, the grant they issued. For Website Chat and the Custom Channel API, the **signing key** the installation will sign its deliveries with. Stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to its tenant, connection and purpose, and never returned by any operation.

appId.description: Legacy/internal UUID of a preconfigured channel app. Browser clients use providerAppId. Do not send both references.

providerAppId.description: The provider-facing Meta App ID shown in Meta Business. It must already be registered in the server installation; the browser never receives the App Secret.

scopes.description: Teams and inboxes the invitee will hold. An inviter may only grant scopes they hold themselves.

DeliveryState.description: What the provider says happened. A separate fact from the command state, folded independently: a receipt never moves this backwards, and one that would have is recorded as an anomaly instead.

Invitation.description: An invitation. The token is NEVER included: it is a credential, delivered out of band, and holding one is how a person becomes a member.

id.description: null only for a tenant scope.

permissions.description: Permission keys held by this membership's role. Conversation scope is still enforced by the server.

id.description: null only for a tenant-wide scope.

OutboundAttempt.description: One network attempt. The row is committed **before** the request leaves, so an attempt with no outcome after a crash is the evidence that the result is unknown.

state_reason.description: A typed reason from the permit or the provider, never free text from a client.

delivery_anomaly.description: Set when a receipt disagreed with what was already known, e.g. `delivered_after_read`. Recorded rather than smoothed over.

OwnershipTransfer.description: An offer the recipient accepts, not something an Owner can do to somebody. One live offer per company.

Person.description: One membership in this company. Administrative fields only; this is not a directory of everything known about a person.

RecoveryAcceptedResponse.description: Identical for a known and an unknown address, and identical when rate limited. Any variation here would be an account-existence oracle.

message.example: If that address has an account, a recovery message has been sent.

token.description: Delivered out of band. Never returned by any endpoint.

Role.description: A tenant role. Authorization is decided by permission key; `name` is a label for humans and is never used in a decision.

RoleGrant.description: A permission this role holds, and how far it reaches. A denial is the ABSENCE of a grant, never a grant with scope 'none'.

RoleGrantWrite.description: `none` is deliberately not a value: a denial is the absence of a grant, and a second spelling would give every reader two things to check.

template.description: Only meaningful where the channel has templates. A template approved for another channel is refused, and a channel with no template concept refuses one outright.

clientMessageId.description: The caller's own id for this message. A retry carrying the same one is the same message, not a second one. Required rather than generated, because a server-generated value would differ on every retry.

trafficClass.description: Which worker pool drains it. Interactive replies and bulk campaigns share one provider rate limit but not one queue.

isPrivateNote.description: An internal note. Accepted by the parser and then refused by the permit with `note_not_deliverable`, so the decision lives in one tested place rather than in a silently dropped field.

archived.description: An archived team keeps its history and takes no new members.

members.description: Who is in the team, so an administrator can see and undo what they added.

TextLimit.description: Both units, because providers publish one or the other and they diverge badly for Arabic: a 1000-character bound is reached at 500 Arabic characters when the real limit is 1000 bytes.

UpdateMembershipRequest.description: Only the fields present are changed. An empty body is rejected: it means the caller believes it changed something.

UpdateTeamRequest.description: A partial patch: an absent field is left alone. At least one field is required.

archived.description: Archiving keeps the team history and stops it taking new members.

WebhookAccepted.description: The ACK means the delivery was journaled durably, and nothing more. Normalization, the inbox and every integration happen afterwards.

duplicates.description: Events already journaled under the same dedupe key. Counted rather than ignored, so redelivery is visible.

maskedLabel.description: Enough of the customer's identity to tell two waiting cards apart, and no more.

version.description: The version to send with a claim. An optimistic-concurrency token, not a fact about the customer: without it the role the queue exists for could not satisfy the version-checked claim (IAM-13).

connectionId.description: The inbox this conversation belongs to.

contactId.description: Resolved from the customer's first message. Null on a conversation opened by an outbound message to somebody nobody has heard from.

pendingReason.description: Why an agent said they were waiting. Present only while the status is `pending`.

snoozeTimezone.description: The IANA zone the wake time was chosen in. Kept beside the instant because the instant cannot say what the operator meant.

unread.description: Whether THIS caller has seen the newest activity. Only the list carries it: unread is a fact about a person, not about the conversation.

ownerState.description: Bot-versus-human ownership (ADR-0008). A different dimension from `status`, from each person’s read cursor and from provider delivery state, and never folded into any of them. No bot exists in this build, so every conversation is `human_active`.

ownerVersion.description: The fence an AI result is re-checked against, at submission and again before dispatch. Bumped by every human ownership change.

version.description: The version shown on the card the agent acted on.

id.description: Stable identity, for deduplicating an at-least-once delivery.

seq.description: Dense per company and issued in commit order, so a gap means a missed event.

payload.description: The event body, or a projected queue card carrying `projected: true` when the caller may only preview this conversation.

cursor.description: Present on stream frames: the position to resume from after this event.

reason.description: Present only when the status is reset_required.

backlog.description: Events still waiting beyond this page.

at.description: The provider's time for an inbound message, ours for an outbound command.

author_membership_id.description: Outbound only: the agent who wrote it.

command_state.description: Outbound only: what we asked the provider to do.

delivery_state.description: Outbound only: what the provider later said happened.

scopeId.description: The channel connection the external id is scoped to. A page-scoped id means nothing outside its page.

validTo.description: Null while the identity is live. Rotation closes an interval and opens a new one rather than overwriting (CT-02).

attributes.description: Business fields, named by the company.

consent.description: Newest first. Present on a single-contact read.

suppressed.description: Channels this contact has opted out on. Outranks any consent above.

ConversationTransitionRequest.description: One of the five agent-driven rows of the conversation lifecycle. `wait` requires a reason, `snooze` a future `wakeAt` and an IANA `timezone`, `resolve` a disposition. The table decides whether the move is legal from the state the conversation is actually in; an illegal one is a 409 naming the reason.

wakeAt.description: Required by `snooze`. Must be in the future and within a year.

timezone.description: Required by `snooze`. An IANA zone name, stored beside the instant.

Episode.description: One reporting episode. A reopened conversation starts a new one and the previous episode's metrics are retained, so a second issue's first-response clock does not start at the first issue's first message.

Note.description: A private note. Internal only: it has no provider, no delivery state and no channel window, and no endpoint can put one on a wire. A deleted note keeps its row and its attribution and loses only its text.

MarkReadRequest.description: Moves only this caller's read cursor. It is not a receipt: nothing here reaches the customer and nothing here changes the conversation's state.

readThrough.description: Absent means now. A time in the future is clamped to now, so a caller cannot claim to have read what has not happened.

version.description: The conversation version the operator saw. A stale one is refused rather than silently taking work from somebody.

assigneeMembershipId.description: Who to give it to. `null` takes it off every desk, which is an operation rather than a missing field.

label.description: The name this company shows for the person. Never their login email.

assigned.description: Whether this person currently holds the conversation.

state.description: While `pending` the current assignee is still the assignee: an unanswered offer is not limbo.

basedOnVersion.description: The conversation version the offer was made against. Acceptance is fenced on the version at acceptance, not on this one.

expiresAt.description: A stored instant swept durably. A browser timer may grey out a button; it never expires an offer.

version.description: The conversation version the requester saw. A stale version is refused.

toMembershipId.description: The colleague being asked. Never yourself.

expiresAt.description: Between five minutes and seven days from now. Absent means one hour.

participated.description: Whether this person actually acted. Removing an invitation cannot undo that, and does not try to.

pending.description: Recipients still planned, queued or in flight.

included.description: Eligible members of the execution audience snapshot; null before launch.

excluded.description: Excluded members of the execution audience snapshot; null before launch.

filters.description: The scope the report was computed over, as requested.

trend.description: Recipients grouped by the UTC day their execution launched, oldest first.
